page.layout: One page of text in one column; running head at top centre; margin notes right (two notes); catchword at lower right. The strip of text at the far left is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: nugas profunderent, & inutili studio tem-pus tererent: cujus calumniæ & nostrum est ferax seculum: Physicos enim vulgò nomi-Physicos moderninari exaudias, qui studijs parum frugiferis operantur, & mentis non vsque ad eò sanæ indicia subinde faciunt: quibus operosè respondere pretium operæ nonduco: Indignos[illegible, ~6 letters] enim eos judico, quibus vel minimus maje-statis Naturæ radius affulgeat. Solis igitur iis, qui etsi Naturæ studium non exagitant, sua-vitatem tamen ejus & vtilitatem non assequun-tur, vtramque studij hujus prærogativam commendatum eo.

Suavitatem naturalis studij eloquaturSuavitas Physi-ci studii nobis divini eloquij vir, Cicero. Est. inquit 2. quæst. Academ. animorum ingeniorum quena-turale quoddam quasi pabulum consideratio con-templatioq; Naturæ. Erigimur, elatiores fieri vi-demur, humana despicimus, cogitantes supera atq; cœlestia: hæc nostra vt exigua & minima conte-mnimus. Indagatio ipsa rerum tum maximarum, tum etiam occultissimarumha bet oblectationem. Si vero aliquid occurrat, quod verisimile videa-tur, humanissimâ completur animus voluptate. Quid dulcius, inquit idem, 2. Tuscul. quæst. otio literario, his dico literis, quibus infinitatem

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "Physicos moderni" in the right margin is partly curved and hard to read; the "moderni" part is doubtful. The mark at "Indignos" in the right margin looks like a handwritten flourish or a stamp rather than printed text; it is marked illegible and may not be printed. The note "Suavitas Physici studii" is set in small curved type and is transcribed as best read. "studijeloquatur" appears run together in the scan; it is given with a space. "occultissimarumha bet" shows a spacing error in the print; it is kept as printed. Sentences in Cicero's quotation are set in italic and may include some roman words. The reference "2." after "inquit" is a small printed number and is kept as printed. "rerum" at the lower right is the catchword, not part of the paragraph.
